title: webgpu: add f16 support to fill/set_rows
author: yomaytk
body:
## Overview

This PR fixes the CI error: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/actions/runs/36983330468/job/110762637185#step:8:12265

In glm5-next, the following two `ggml_fill` nodes and the `ggml_set_rows` node (in `build_kpool_select`) operate on f16 tensors when FA is enabled. Since the WebGPU backend only supported f32 for FILL and f32 as the source type for SET_ROWS, they were assigned to the CPU backend. This PR adds f16 support for both so that they now run on WebGPU, which fixes the error.

```cpp
ggml_tensor * mask_all = ggml_new_tensor_4d(ctx0, kq_mask->type, n_kv + n_sel, 1, 1, 1);
mask_all = ggml_fill(ctx0, mask_all, -INFINITY);
...
ggml_tensor * zeros = ggml_new_tensor_4d(ctx0, kq_mask->type, n_sel, 1, 1, 1);
zeros = ggml_fill(ctx0, zeros, 0.0f);
...
ggml_tensor * sel = ggml_set_rows(ctx0, mask_all, zeros, ggml_reshape_3d(ctx0, sel_idx, n_sel, n_tokens, 1));
```

title: webgpu : fix race condition in memset
author: eapache
body:
## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->
#31157 enabled automatic parallel test workers. This exposed an existing race in the WebGPU backend in CI, e.g. https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/actions/runs/40218104124/job/121243543710

Concurrent calls to `ggml_backend_webgpu_buffer_memset`  can race between setting and using the shared `memset_params_buf`. Fix by guarding with the existing mutex.

This showed up in CI consistently with the Grok fragmented KV-cache test. I didn't check this part, but apparently it showed up here specifically because "Grok runs without flash attention, so its transposed f16 value-cache writes can require small, unaligned updates".

A few quick perf checks did not reveal any regressions from using the lock here.

## Requirements

<!-- IMPORTANT: Please do NOT delete this section, otherwise your PR may be rejected -->

comments.body: @yomaytk Such a global mutex seems a bit strange - is it really necessary to have it? Which part of WebGPU makes it necessary?
comments.author: ggerganov

comments.body:
> @yomaytk Such a global mutex seems a bit strange - is it really necessary to have it? Which part of WebGPU makes it necessary?

Thanks, good catch. After this PR is merged, this global mutex is necessary for `memset` and `get_tensor` to avoid conflicts when accessing the intermediate buffers defined in the global context struct. But we can define those buffers and locks in the buffer context struct, which holds the actual buffer of `ggml_backend_buffer_t`, and it would be better than having a global lock.
On the other hand, it seems that Vulkan uses a [mutex defined in the device struct in functions such as get_tensor](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/c6fb3b5be2209f6c12339833198190f6f6829581/ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan-buffers.cpp#L735), so there might be a reason for this design.

If it looks good, I'll open a follow-up PR to address this and check it with the tests.

title: ggml: support non-contiguous SUM (CPU, CUDA, Vulkan, WebGPU)
author: rssndr
body:
## Overview

`test-backend-ops` includes `SUM(type=f32,ne=[33,256,1,1],permute=[1,0,2,3])`, which CUDA rejects and which crashes the CPU reference if enabled. Changes:
- CUDA: `supports_op` required `ggml_is_contiguous_rows`, but the kernel only requires `ggml_is_contiguously_allocated` (asserted in `ggml_cuda_op_sum` since #10544). The flat CUB reduction is valid for any gap-free view, since summation is order-independent. The `contiguous_rows` check was added in #16559 to keep CI green after that PR introduced permuted SUM test cases, it wasn't based on what the CUDA kernel can actually handle. This change makes `supports_op` match the condition the kernel itself asserts. The kernel is unchanged.
- CPU: `ggml_compute_forward_sum_f32` asserted `nb[0] == sizeof(float)`, so it aborted on non-contiguous rows, reached as soon as the CPU acts as reference (or fallback) for this case. Added a strided path keeping `ggml_float` accumulation; contiguous fast path unchanged. f16/bf16 variants left as-is.
- Vulkan: `supports_op` accepted SUM for any input with contiguous rows, but the kernel sums the tensor as a single flat block, so sliced views returned wrong results. Changed the check to `ggml_is_contiguously_allocated`, matching the CUDA fix (per 0cc4m’s go-ahead).
- WebGPU: same gate/kernel mismatch as Vulkan (flat sum over a view with gaps). Same fix, per yomaytk’s go-ahead.

*Why CPU and CUDA together* : the CPU fix is required for the CUDA case to be testable, since the reference crashes once the case is enabled.

## Additional information

Testing (RTX 3070 Ti Laptop, CUDA 13.3):
- `test-backend-ops -o SUM`: all cases pass on CUDA and Vulkan (Intel Iris Xe + NVIDIA via Vulkan). The sliced-view cases are correctly reported as not supported
- `test-backend-ops grad -o SUM`: pass
- WebGPU not tested locally; verified by CI
- `perf -o SUM`: unchanged

Ref #14909, #16559, #28175.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES. Used Claude for analysis help, code drafting for the CPU change, and the initial description draft. Reviewed, built, and tested locally.
